functions.description: Parse a monetary amount text with currency symbol and scale word into an exact Decimal dollar amount
inputs: monetary amount as text copied from the question with currency symbol and scale word
outputs: amount in dollars as an exact Decimal

functions.description: Parse a count of years written as digits or English number words into an integer.
inputs: number of years as text copied from the question
outputs: whole number of years as an integer

functions.description: Compute the double-declining-balance rate as two divided by the useful life in years.
inputs: useful life of the asset in years
outputs: double-declining-balance rate as an exact fraction

functions.description: Cap a candidate depreciation charge so the resulting book value does not fall below salvage value, parsing each dollar input robustly first.
inputs: candidate depreciation charge in dollars
beginning book value for the year in dollars
salvage value in dollars

functions.description: Compute the straight-line depreciation charge for the year on the remaining depreciable base over the remaining years
inputs: beginning book value for the year in dollars
salvage value in dollars
remaining useful life in years including the current year
outputs: straight-line charge for the year in dollars

functions.description: Compute one year of double-declining-balance depreciation as the larger of the declining-balance and straight-line charges, capped so book value stays at or above salvage, and return the charge and year-end book value.
inputs: beginning book value for the year in dollars
salvage value in dollars
double-declining-balance rate as an exact fraction
remaining useful life in years including the current year
outputs: depreciation charge for the year in dollars
book value at year end in dollars

functions.description: Simulate year-by-year double-declining-balance depreciation with salvage floor to find the book value after a number of years.
inputs: asset cost in dollars
salvage value in dollars
useful life in years
number of elapsed years
double-declining-balance rate as an exact fraction
outputs: book value after the elapsed years in dollars

functions.description: Format a dollar book value rounded half-up to cents for the final answer.
inputs: book value after the elapsed years in dollars
outputs: formatted book value in dollars to two decimal places

functions.description: Compute the book value after a given number of years under double-declining-balance depreciation with a salvage floor by parsing the inputs and simulating year by year.
inputs: the original cost of the asset in dollars, as text copied from the question including currency symbol and any scale word
the useful life of the asset in years, as text copied from the question
the salvage (residual) value of the asset at the end of its useful life in dollars, as text copied from the question
the number of years elapsed since acquisition at which the book value is required, as text copied from the question
outputs: final book value after the elapsed years, formatted in dollars to two decimal places

functions.description: Parse a raw quantity text into its numeric magnitude with any scale word applied and its unit symbol.
inputs: quantity as raw text copied from the question

functions.description: Convert a container volume text into cubic metres using exact unit factors.
inputs: the volume of the flask or container holding the gas with unit

functions.description: Convert an amount of substance given as raw text into moles using exact unit factors.
inputs: the amount of gas in moles with unit

functions.description: Convert a temperature text with unit into kelvin, applying the Celsius or Fahrenheit offset when needed and rejecting non-physical values.
inputs: the temperature of the gas with unit

functions.description: Apply the ideal gas law to compute pressure in pascals from amount in moles, temperature in kelvin and volume in cubic metres
inputs: amount of substance in moles
temperature in kelvin
volume in cubic metres

functions.description: Convert a pressure given in pascals into bar using the exact factor 1 bar = 100000 Pa.
inputs: pressure in pascals

functions.description: Compute the pressure of a perfect gas in bar from the container volume, the amount of gas and its temperature.
inputs: the volume of the flask or container holding the gas with unit
the amount of gas in moles with unit
the name or chemical formula of the gas
the temperature of the gas with unit
outputs: pressure of the gas in bar

entry_points.text: Using the double-declining-balance method, find the book value after ●4 of an asset that cost ●1, has a ●2 and a ●3 salvage value.

params.description: the original cost of the asset in dollars, as text copied from the question including currency symbol and any scale word
params.validity_range: Must be a positive monetary amount, strictly greater than the salvage value (●3); if cost equals salvage there is no depreciable base and the book value is constant. Scale words k, thousand, million, billion multiply by 10^3, 10^3, 10^6, 10^9 respectively.

params.description: the useful life of the asset in years, as text copied from the question
params.validity_range: Must be a positive integer number of years (at least 1). The DDB rate 2/life is defined only for life ≥ 1; the life also sets the number of remaining years used in the straight-line switch test.

params.description: the salvage (residual) value of the asset at the end of its useful life in dollars, as text copied from the question
params.validity_range: Must be a non-negative monetary amount, less than the cost (●1). A salvage of zero is valid and means depreciation continues down to zero book value.

params.description: the number of years elapsed since acquisition at which the book value is required, as text copied from the question
params.validity_range: Must be a non-negative whole number of years. Values from 0 up to the useful life (●2) are standard; beyond the useful life the book value is held at the salvage floor and the result is salvage value.

entry_points.text: A ●1 flask holds ●2 of ●3 at ●4. Assuming perfect-gas behaviour, what pressure does the gas exert?

params.description: the volume of the flask or container holding the gas with unit
params.validity_range: Strictly positive finite volume; any unit with a known exact factor to cubic metres (L, mL, dm3, cm3, m3) is valid, and zero or negative volume is physically impossible and must be rejected.

params.description: the amount of gas in moles with unit
params.validity_range: Non-negative finite amount of substance; zero gives zero pressure and negative amounts are unphysical. Units must be convertible to moles (mol, mmol, kmol).

params.description: the name or chemical formula of the gas
params.validity_range: Any substance treated as a perfect gas at the stated conditions; the ideal gas law is accurate only away from condensation and at low to moderate pressure, and the identity of the gas does not change the calculation under the perfect-gas assumption.

params.description: the temperature of the gas with unit
params.validity_range: Must be above absolute zero: strictly positive in kelvin, or above -273.15 °C, or above -459.67 °F; kelvin, Celsius and Fahrenheit are valid units with their offsets applied before use.
